questions.answer:
Operator: create evidence records and see save/failure outcomes
Reviewer: inspect evidence categories and status summaries

Evidence creation is visible, persisted, and traceable through telemetry.
Invalid evidence submissions are blocked without database writes.
Reviewers can see represented and missing validation categories.
Persistence failures are visible and do not masquerade as successful saves.

EvidenceRecord: draft -> validated -> persisted
EvidenceRecord: draft -> rejected
EvidenceDashboard: empty -> editing -> saving -> success
EvidenceDashboard: editing -> validation_error
EvidenceDashboard: saving -> persistence_failure

The UI never writes directly to SQLite and must call interface/application code.
CreateEvidence persists through a repository port backed by the SQLite adapter.
Data-changing browser validation uses an isolated SQLite test database copy.
Successful create emits evidence_create_started and evidence_create_succeeded telemetry.
Validation and persistence failures emit failure telemetry and do not persist a successful evidence row.

FLOW-001 Operator creates evidence: open /evidence -> submit valid title category and status -> repository inserts one EvidenceRecord in the isolated SQLite test database -> UI shows success and the new row -> telemetry records evidence_create_started and evidence_create_succeeded
FLOW-002 Operator sees validation errors: open /evidence -> submit missing required fields -> application validation rejects the command -> UI shows field errors -> no EvidenceRecord is inserted
FLOW-003 Reviewer inspects evidence categories: seed isolated SQLite test database with evidence rows -> open /evidence -> list evidence records -> summarize represented and missing categories -> reviewer sees category status summaries
FLOW-004 Persistence failure is visible: enable repository write failure flag -> submit valid evidence -> SQLite adapter rejects the write -> UI shows failure state -> no saved row appears -> telemetry records database_write_failed and evidence_create_failed

tests/e2e/evidence.spec.ts::operator creates evidence proves FLOW-001 UI, database, and telemetry behavior.
tests/e2e/evidence.spec.ts::operator sees validation errors proves FLOW-002 validation behavior.
tests/e2e/evidence.spec.ts::reviewer inspects evidence categories proves FLOW-003 reviewer behavior.
tests/e2e/evidence.spec.ts::persistence failure is visible proves FLOW-004 failure behavior.
Vitest unit and integration tests prove domain, application, SQLite repository, and telemetry adapter behavior.

FLOW-001 inserts one evidence record into the isolated SQLite evidence table.
FLOW-002 performs no database mutation.
FLOW-003 seeds representative evidence rows in the isolated SQLite test database before read-only inspection.
FLOW-004 rejects the attempted insert and persists no new evidence row.

Domain entities and validation rules have no dependency on React, HTTP, SQLite, filesystem telemetry, or Playwright.
Application use cases depend on repository and telemetry ports.
SQLite and JSONL telemetry are replaceable adapters.
HTTP and React interfaces delegate to application use cases instead of owning business rules.
Tests exercise domain/application contracts before adapter and UI behavior.
